world_reference.note: The working pack supplied this root-world UUID but no corresponding entity. It is retained only for relational compatibility and must not be interpreted as canon.

entries.Name: The Pale Reef of Relay Twelve
entries.Description: A memory-centred continuity station whose cooling structure gradually became architecture, habitat, and sacred boundary. Its keepers treat quiet operation as proof of careful custody because vibration and signal noise once damaged fragile identity systems.

provenance.note: The pack attributes a pale archive reef and radiator fins to V11, but the cited manuscript is unavailable. The name and particulars are new V12 candidates.

servati.editorial_notes: DRAFT candidate; not present as a verified named entity in the repository baseline.

entries.Name: The Ash Roads of Transfer Cluster K-6
entries.Description: A matter-first Lamp built through a mined asteroid. Burden movement remains physical and slow. Route gradients, resting thresholds, and load scars become the culture's most trusted historical evidence.

provenance.note: The pack attributes a dust-choked asteroid Lamp to V11, but the cited manuscript is unavailable. The name and particulars are new V12 candidates.

entries.Name: The Drowned Threshold of Pelagic Vault Seven
entries.Description: A flooded custody complex whose inhabitants adapt to pressure, darkness, and submerged access. Here, approach is part of truth: a record removed from its depth, route, and threshold is considered dangerously incomplete.

provenance.note: The pack attributes a drowned-moon Lamp and pressure-adapted custodians to V11, but the cited manuscript is unavailable. The name and particulars are new V12 candidates.

entries.Name: The Unopened Spring of Seed Reserve Thirty-One
entries.Description: A seed reserve whose activation rules outlive the civilisation that wrote them. Its culture grows around maintaining viability while debating whether any surviving authority can honestly declare the required future conditions satisfied.

provenance.note: The pack attributes embryo-preserving Seed Lamps with obsolete release conditions to V11, but the cited manuscript is unavailable. The name and particulars are new V12 candidates.

entries.Name: The Corridor of No Arrival
entries.Description: A route-centred culture that continues maintaining a transfer corridor after its traffic disappears. Correct passage becomes the inheritance itself: markers are repaired, gradients checked, and receiving intervals opened even when nothing arrives.

provenance.note: The pack attributes route Lamps maintaining unused beacon corridors to V11, but the cited manuscript is unavailable. The name and particulars are new V12 candidates.

entries.Name: The Broken Frame Concordance at Transfer Site Nine
entries.Description: A rare mixed Lamp formed around a disaster site where damaged burden frames, partial names, and broken relation fields could not be reconciled honestly. Its keepers preserve fragments side by side rather than constructing a false single account.

provenance.note: The pack attributes mixed sites, damaged frames, fragmentary records, and later purification risks to V11, but the cited manuscript is unavailable. The name and particulars are new V12 candidates.

servati.editorial_notes: DRAFT candidate; not present as a verified named entity in the repository baseline.

entries.Name: The Partition of Transfer Site Nine
entries.Description: Three custody authorities attempt to separate a mixed relic complex into matter, record, and pattern holdings. The Concordance refuses because the relations among the fragments are themselves evidence. The attempted partition damages the comparison field even though most physical material survives.

Nature.history: DRAFT event grounded by the working pack in its claim that V11 describes mixed sites being divided, purified, or destroyed during Custody Wars.
Nature.consequences: Becomes a candidate example of why preserving objects while severing relations can still constitute catastrophic loss.

provenance.note: The claimed conflict type needs checking against V11; the named incident is a new V12 candidate.

servati.editorial_notes: DRAFT event; no chronology date is assigned.

entries.Name: The False Release at Seed Reserve Thirty-One
entries.Description: A release authorisation reaches the reserve carrying valid-looking procedural structure but incompatible provenance. One faction argues that delay is killing the future; another argues that activation under false authority would be irreversible violation.

Nature.history: DRAFT event grounded by the working pack in its claim that V11 names false release orders and conflicts over seed activation.
Nature.consequences: The reserve remains closed, but trust in remote authorisation collapses and later Seed communities require stronger plural verification.

provenance.note: The claimed conflict type needs checking against V11; the named incident is a new V12 candidate.

entries.Name: The Silence Breach of Relay Twelve
entries.Description: An outside order forces a high-energy witness transmission through Relay Twelve, claiming that untransmitted identities are being abandoned. The local keepers argue the signal itself destabilises fragile relation fields.

Nature.history: DRAFT event grounded by the working pack in its claim that V11 contrasts quiet record cultures with emission traditions and describes forced access.
Nature.consequences: Some names are broadcast successfully; other uncertainty structures are damaged. Both sides preserve evidence supporting their accusation.

entries.Name: The Redirection of the Ash Convoy
entries.Description: Two matter-custody orders claim the same convoy. Neither side wants to damage the burdens, so the conflict becomes a slow contest of route authority, frame control, and lawful handoff rather than conventional battle.

Nature.history: DRAFT event grounded by the working pack in its claim that V11 describes opposing Pallbearer orders redirecting a sealed convoy without breaking vibration law.
Nature.consequences: The burdens survive, but their route provenance fractures into incompatible records that later communities cannot fully reconcile.

entries.Name: The Drowned Marker Seizure
entries.Description: A rival authority removes submerged route markers from Pelagic Vault Seven, claiming the markers unlawfully bind later transfers to a dead spatial doctrine. Local custodians treat removal as destruction of historical relation.

Nature.history: DRAFT event grounded by the working pack in its claim that V11 describes conflicts over submerged route markers in drowned reliquary seas.
Nature.consequences: The recovered markers survive physically, but their original currents, depths, and approach geometry cannot be recreated elsewhere.

entries.Name: The Index Without Uncertainty
entries.Description: A copied identity archive is deliberately simplified so every record resolves to one answer. The copy is easier to use and spreads rapidly. Its missing uncertainty fields are discovered only after it has become the basis for transfers across multiple sites.

Nature.history: DRAFT event grounded by the working pack in its claim that V11 describes archives stripped of uncertainty and the resulting false certainty.
Nature.consequences: Later custody decisions may be internally consistent but historically untrustworthy. No surviving authority can fully reconstruct which corrections were lost.
